subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex real-time quoting (post-call)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@finex.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Sep 10, 2026 at 3:20 PM PDT
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex real-time quoting (post-call)

Hi Tom / Sasha —

Thanks for the time today — great call. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can produce a throughput sizing estimate: 

Summary of the integration we want to size
- Feature: real-time quote generation (streaming partial responses to UI) and a small batch fallback for heavy-load reconciliation.
- Primary SLOs: first-byte/streaming latency target ~≤250–350 ms (95th) for interactive flows; end-to-end generation for long responses can be higher.

Questions / data we need (please confirm the numbers below if I heard correctly):
1) Steady-state QPS: ~150 QPS
2) Peak QPS (burst): ~900 QPS (bursts typically 5–15 minutes, daily peak windows)
3) Average response size: ~200–300 tokens (you said ~250 tokens average)
4) Streaming: required (we need partial tokens streamed to the UI as they are generated)
5) Concurrent inflight requests during peak: ~1,000–1,200

Action items from Redwood:
- We’ll run a preliminary tokens/sec and QPS-based compute estimate and return a sizing recommendation (dedicated pool vs. hosted burst/overflow).
- Rafael will scope batch/streaming tradeoffs and quantization options for cost vs latency.

I’ve attached the workbook you shared and our call notes (finex_workload_metrics.xlsx). If any of the numbers above are off, reply with corrections — especially peak duration and average tokens per request since those affect tokens/sec calculation a lot.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sizing follow-up with Rafael and me next week. Are you available Tue/Wed morning PST?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

Attachments: finex_workload_metrics.xlsx

From: Tom Li <tom.li@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@finex.com>
Date: Fri, Sep 11, 2026 at 9:05 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex real-time quoting (post-call)

Thanks Neha — quick confirmations and a couple of clarifications below. Numbers are correct with small caveats:

- Steady-state QPS: 130–160 QPS (150 is a good nominal)
- Peak QPS: up to ~900 QPS. Peaks are usually short (5–15 minutes). We see ~3–4 of these peaks per day during market hours.
- Avg tokens/request: 220–280 tokens; 250 is a fair average. Some longer requests (ad hoc explainers) can be ~800 tokens but those are <1% of traffic.
- Streaming: yes — the front-end needs partial content as it generates (first-byte latency matters). Ideally first-token streaming latency 95th ≤ 250 ms.
- Concurrency: Peak inflight requests ~1,050; tokenization and post-processing add ~10–50 ms per request.

I’ve attached an anonymized sample payloads file from our logs (finex_sample_payloads.json). Also, we’re evaluating a soft SLO: for the <1% long requests we accept up to 1.5–2s p95.

Availability: Tue 9–11am PST or Wed 10–12pm PST works.

—Tom Li
Senior Product Manager, Finex
tom.li@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@finex.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Sep 11, 2026 at 11:30 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex real-time quoting (post-call)

Tom / Neha — thanks for the details, this is helpful. Based on the numbers you confirmed, here are a few quick, preliminary sizing notes so you have context before the follow-up call: 

Preliminary compute math (ballpark):
- Peak tokens/sec estimate = peak QPS * avg tokens/request = 900 * 250 = 225,000 tokens/sec
- Steady-state tokens/sec = 150 * 250 = 37,500 tokens/sec
- Concurrent inflight ~1,050 (as reported) — important for memory/KV-cache sizing for cached prefix workloads.

Implications / quick sizing guidance:
- Streaming SLO (95th first-byte ≤250 ms) implies we should prioritize lower-latency model variants and avoid large batch windows for interactive traffic. Continuous batching at small intervals (e.g., 10–30 ms) is usually best to keep latency predictable while still getting batching efficiency.
- For the peak tokens/sec at 225k, we’ll evaluate two approaches: 1) Dedicated GPU pool sized for peak with autoscale headroom and burst policy; or 2) Hybrid: smaller dedicated pool for steady-state + fast burst capacity (hosted) for peaks — more cost-efficient but slightly more complex for failover.
- Quantization: moving to int8/4-bit variants can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput; we’ll include perf profiles for the model family you’ll run.

Questions before the sizing call:
1) Which model family are you planning to run in prod (open model name/version)?
2) Do you expect a high prefix cache hit rate (many requests reuse common prompts) or is each request largely unique?
3) Any traffic shaping required per customer (are some customers prioritized)?

I attached a short PDF with the rough tokens/sec to GPU estimate we use internally (redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf). Happy to walk through it on the call and make it concrete with your model choice + token distribution.

Proposed meeting: Tue 9:30–10:00am PST (fits both windows) — marking tentative.

Thanks,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_throughput_estimate.pdf

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

2) Confirmed call: Tue Sep 15, 2026 at 9:30 AM PST — calendar invite to follow.
3) Please upload the model name/version you plan to use to the shared Drive folder so we can prepare perf profiles.

If anything changes on the token distribution or expected peak durations, let us know before the call. Looking forward to the sizing session.

Best,
Neha
